workingTitle: Webb reads a star's final mixing in Cassiopeia A's dust
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed Astrophysical Journal Letters article and NASA/ESA science releases published November 23, 2026
coreFacts: JWST's MIRI Medium-resolution Spectrometer isolated mid-infrared dust spectra from three individual clumps in the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant.
One argon-bright reverse-shocked ejecta clump was dominated by silica dust, while a neon-bright, carbon-monoxide-rich ejecta clump was dominated by carbon dust.
The Green Monster region, made from material shed before the explosion, was rich in complex magnesium silicates.
Mapping those spectral templates across the remnant showed shell-merger signatures over much of Cassiopeia A.
The authors interpret the chemistry as evidence that burning shells inside the progenitor star mixed shortly before core collapse.
